newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan sees no anthrax worry in Australia milk, beef.
newsitem.headline: Japan sees no anthrax worry in Australia milk, beef.

text.p: Japan remained satisfied with Australia's response to a limited outbreak of anthrax among dairy cattle and saw no need to limit Australian beef or dairy product imports, a Health Ministry official said on Thursday.
"We have concluded that there is no reason to believe that beef or dairy products infected with anthrax will be imported," the official said.

"We have looked into the matter and the Australian government has looked into the matter, and an Australian minister has announced that beef products and dairy products were both absolutely safe," she added.
She said that, according to information from the Australian Embassy and other sources, only dairy cattle were affected and any anthrax in dairy products would be destroyed through processing.

She also said Japan received assurances that vaccinations were carried out in areas around the infected infected region, that carcasses of infected cattle were disposed of properly and that an Australian man infected with anthrax had recovered.

A spokesman for Australia's Department of Natural Resources and Environment said on Tuesday that the number of infected properties in northern Victoria had risen to 61, up from 52 on Monday, and that 121 cattle had died from the disease, up from 105 the day before. The infected area supplies about 30 percent of Australia's dairy products.

Japan imported 49,694 tonnes of cheese and 11,760 tonnes of powdered skim milk from Australia in the first 11 months of 1996, according to the latest government data. Japan also imports frozen and refrigerated beef from Australia.
South Korea's Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry said on Thursday it asked Australia to halt exports of beef from anthrax-hit areas slaughtered after January 26.
